Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a short list of clarifying questions so we can recommend the right onramp: 

What we covered:
- Demo of Redwood Hosted API: streaming responses, endpoint perms, token/usage analytics
- Failure/fallback story: how we route to compatible variants and maintain availability
- High-level difference between Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Private VPC/on-prem

Clarifying questions for you (helps us recommend next steps):
1) Data residency: you mentioned EU residency is required — can you confirm whether data at rest AND inference telemetry must remain in EU?
2) Latency SLO: you noted low latency is important. What's your SLO (P50/P95 target)? Any strict sub-200ms requirement?
3) Traffic profile: expected concurrent sessions and peak RPS during end-of-month spikes? Average request size (tokens)?
4) Security evidence: do you need SOC 2 + audit logs + KMS/HSM integration for keys?

Suggested immediate next steps (we can move fast once we have answers):
- If EU residency + standard SOC2 is sufficient: enable a Hosted EU evaluation workspace and a 30–90 day quickstart (no infra install).
- If you require contractual data isolation/SLA: we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved) or Private VPC for air-gapped requirements — we can scope effort and timelines.

I've attached a short quickstart checklist and a preliminary pricing estimate so you can see the cost/step tradeoffs. If you prefer, we can schedule a short 30-minute technical follow-up with Marissa (solutions) to map traffic and validate latency with a small-scale load test.

Thanks — talk soon,

Thanks Avery — great demo, and appreciated the clear breakdown. Short answers below and a couple of asks from our security/compliance team.

Answers:
- Data residency: we need both data at rest and inference telemetry (logs/metrics) retained in EU (preferably in an EU region with contractual commitments).
- Latency SLO: target P95 <= 200ms for inference (critical for user-facing flows).
- Traffic profile: average session ~12 tokens output, bursts up to ~500 req/s for a 10–15 minute period at month-end; steady-state ~40–60 req/s.
- Security evidence: SOC2 report is required; we also need audit log access and key control (KMS). Integration with our IdP (SAML) would be nice but not mandatory for the pilot.

Constraints / asks:
- Contracting lead time is a factor — we typically need 4–6 weeks for procurement. Would you be able to put a short evaluation contract / MPA in place for a Hosted EU trial while we run procurement for Dedicated if needed?
- Can you share a short expected cost delta between Hosted EU evaluation (metered) and a minimal Dedicated commit that would meet 500 RPS peaks?

I've attached our security questionnaire so Marissa can take a look.

Best,

Thanks for the flag, Avery — good signals from FinSec. Quick take and recommended path to keep momentum: 

Short answer on latency / capacity:
- For short outputs (12 tokens avg) and the stated peaks, Hosted EU (eu-west-1) can often meet sub-200ms P95 for baseline traffic, but burst windows of 500 RPS will likely need either burst capacity (pre-warmed) or a small Dedicated reserve to guarantee the SLA during spikes. We don't recommend relying on ungated Hosted bursting for strict P95 guarantees.

Recommended immediate plan (min friction):
1) Offer a 60-day Hosted EU evaluation workspace under an evaluation MPA (30–90 day option). This lets them validate integration, correctness, and basic latency under normal load. We can temporarily enable EU-only routing and provide SOC2 docs and audit-log access.
2) Parallel: prepare a minimal Dedicated proposal sized for their 500 RPS peak (we'll size GPUs + batch/multiplexing). This will be a reserved-commit option with faster warm-up and clearer SLA.
3) Run one proof-of-concept load test (Marissa to run with their sample traffic) to measure real P95 and validate whether Hosted with warmers is sufficient.

Action items / owners:
- Marissa: can you draft the test plan (targeted load profile, sample payloads, metrics to capture) and review FinSec's security questionnaire? (ETA: 48h)
- Avery: I'll work with legal on a short evaluation MPA template (EU pin + SOC2 clauses) and share a redline-ready doc.
- Ben: I'll get with infra to draft a minimal Dedicated commit estimate and put a preliminary pricing bucket on it (APAC/EU adjustments).

Notes on contracting / procurement:
- We can support a short evaluation MPA that is minimal risk; procurement timelines are realistic. The MPA would include EU-region pinning, data retention terms, and a clear exit window.
- Pricing delta: preliminary rule-of-thumb — metered Hosted evaluation will be lower upfront but higher at sustained peak; Dedicated commit reduces per-token cost by ~35–50% depending on utilization. I'll attach a sample bucket estimate once infra confirms sizing.

Marissa — please confirm when you have time to kick off the load test and I'll follow up with the legal contact for the MPA. Avery — I'll join the next call with FinSec if they want to coordinate procurement or technical questions.
